provides: AI-powered content translation: a TranslationEntry/TranslationValue store across a configurable language set, an LLM-routed translate.resolve comm Function with English-fallback, autofill/verification workflows, a staff dashboard (stats, per-language editing, LLM help, export/import, orphan cleanup), a Figma plugin API, and pluggable key collectors (backend error keys, notification templates, project-specific) so keys enter without any module importing another.

curated.summary: Which backend performs a single-string translation for translate/verify/autofill. Default routes to stapel-agent by HTTP; CommAgentProvider routes through the llm.complete comm Function instead (in-process in a monolith); OpenAICompatibleProvider talks to any OpenAI-compatible endpoint directly (conf.py, MODULE.md Settings table).
Source/fallback language for translate.resolve and autofill (conf.py, MODULE.md Settings table).

Who may call POST translate/api/v1/text/ (dotted DRF permission paths, ALL must pass). The default refuses anonymous callers because every cache miss spends real money on an LLM budget; a public storefront that wants a translate button for logged-out readers sets AllowAny and leans on TEXT_ANON_THROTTLE, a paid product tightens it to its own plan gate. Either way it is settings, not a view subclass (conf.py, views.py TextTranslationView.get_permissions).

Length ceiling per text on POST text/, in characters. Above it the endpoint answers error.400.translate.text_too_long — its own code, so a client can offer to trim rather than retry. The bound exists because an LLM bills by token and one pasted document is an unbounded bill (conf.py, text.check_bounds).
curated.business_label: Longest text that may be translated

curated.summary: How long a translated string is remembered (seconds), keyed by a digest of source, target, context hint and text — so the same listing description translated for a thousand readers is one provider call. 0 disables the cache: a cost decision, not a correctness one (conf.py, text.translate_texts).

extension_points.name: LLM_PROVIDER
extension_points.summary: Resolved via import_string in get_llm_provider(); contract: translate(key, english_text, target_language, context) -> str; subclass providers.BaseTranslationProvider to reuse prompt building (conf.py, MODULE.md 'Settings').

extension_points.name: collectors
extension_points.summary: register_collector('name', callable_or_dotted_path) (collectors.py): a zero-arg callable returning a stats dict, run by collect_translations and the dashboard 'Collect keys' button — the project-specific-keys channel (MODULE.md 'Adding / overriding translations').

extension_points.name: serializer_seams
extension_points.summary: mixins.SerializerSeamMixin: views declare request_serializer_class/response_serializer_class (or purpose-prefixed variants) instantiated only through matching get_*_serializer_class() getters (MODULE.md 'Serializer seams').

extension_points.name: translate.resolve
extension_points.summary: Provided Function: {keys, language} -> {values}, DEFAULT_LANGUAGE fallback, missing keys omitted (never null), soft-deleted entries never resolved (functions.py, MODULE.md 'Functions').

extension_points.name: BaseTranslationProvider.complete
extension_points.summary: The generic half of the LLM_PROVIDER seam: complete(prompt) -> str. A provider that implements it gets batch content translation in ONE upstream call (the content prompt asks for a JSON array and providers.parse_content_batch validates the shape before anything is zipped back onto the inputs); one that implements only the historical translate(key, english_text, target_language, context) keeps working, one call per string (providers.py, MODULE.md 'Content translation').

surface.name: autofill_missing
surface.intent: Fill missing (key, language) translation values via the configured LLM provider, writing verified=False and a TranslationHistory row per fill. This is the core logic behind the translate.autofill comm task and the autofill_translations command — call it directly instead of looping get_llm_provider().translate() yourself when triggering autofill from custom code (e.g. right after a new language is added). Every run is bounded: limit=None means the AUTOFILL_MAX_VALUES ceiling rather than the whole catalogue times every language, and a larger limit is clamped to it, so the returned stats carry the limit actually applied.

surface.name: autofill_targets
surface.intent: The configured languages eligible for autofill (every supported language except the source/default one, optionally narrowed to a caller-given subset). Use this instead of filtering get_supported_languages() yourself so a custom autofill trigger agrees with the built-in task/command on which languages are ever auto-translated.

surface.name: get_collectors
surface.intent: {name: callable} for every registered collector, dotted-path entries resolved on access. Call this instead of reaching into the module's internal registry dict directly when building a custom key-collection command or UI.

surface.name: register_collector
surface.intent: Register a translation-key collector (a zero-arg callable returning a stats dict) under a name — the fork-free way to make collect_translations and the dashboard's 'Collect keys' button pick up a project-specific key source, alongside the built-in errors/notifications collectors.

surface.name: get_default_language
surface.intent: The source/fallback language code (DEFAULT_LANGUAGE) — call this instead of hardcoding 'en' or reading translate_settings.DEFAULT_LANGUAGE directly; translate.resolve, autofill and the dashboard all derive their fallback from this single call.

surface.name: get_language_names
surface.intent: {code: display name} for every configured language, with DEFAULT_LANGUAGE_NAMES filling in any configured code that has no override. Use this instead of reading translate_settings.LANGUAGE_NAMES directly when rendering a language picker, so an unnamed configured language still gets a sensible label instead of a KeyError or a blank.

surface.name: get_supported_languages
surface.intent: The configured language codes. Call this instead of reading translate_settings.LANGUAGES (or django.conf.settings.LANGUAGES) directly: it detects and discards Django's own untouched global LANGUAGES default — which AppSettings' flat-setting fallback would otherwise pick up as if it were a deliberate override — and unwraps Django-style (code, name) tuples.

surface.name: collect_error_keys_from_services
surface.intent: Fan out to every registered service's error-keys endpoint (with per-service mount-point discovery) and upsert TranslationEntry rows tagged source='backend:errors', clearing stale refs first. This is what the 'errors' collector and the dashboard's key-collection button run — call it directly instead of writing your own peer-discovery loop over stapel_core.django.nav.get_services().

surface.name: collect_notification_keys
surface.intent: Fetch the notifications service's notification-keys endpoint (with mount-point discovery, cached per process) and upsert TranslationEntry rows tagged source='backend:notifications'. This is what the 'notifications' collector runs — call it directly instead of hand-rolling the same peer-discovery + upsert logic; NOTIFICATION_KEYS_PATHS already carries the pre-/post-v1-canon mount-point history so a resolver-404 fails loudly (PeerRouteUnavailable) rather than silently reporting zero keys.

surface.name: IsAuthorizedTranslator
surface.intent: DRF permission gate for the translator/dashboard API surface: passes for staff/superusers or any email listed in AuthorizedTranslator with is_active=True. Put this on any endpoint that exposes translation content for editing instead of hand-rolling an is_staff check or a custom AuthorizedTranslator query — it is exactly the check the built-in dashboard and Figma-plugin views already share.

surface.name: can_edit_language
surface.intent: Whether a user may edit/verify a given language — the one call the dashboard/Figma views make before accepting a translation write. Reach for this instead of re-deriving it from get_user_allowed_languages() in a new endpoint; a per-view reimplementation is exactly how a translator-scoping gap would slip past one endpoint and not the others.

surface.name: get_translator_info
surface.intent: Look up the AuthorizedTranslator record for a user by email (None if unauthenticated or not registered). Call this instead of AuthorizedTranslator.objects.get(email=...) directly — it already absorbs the anonymous-user and DoesNotExist cases a naive lookup would need to special-case.

surface.name: get_translator_name
surface.intent: Display name for translation-history logging: the AuthorizedTranslator's name, else the user's full name/email, else empty. Use this instead of user.get_full_name() directly so history entries stay attributable even for a translator record with no linked platform account.

surface.name: get_user_allowed_languages
surface.intent: The language whitelist a user may edit/verify — ALL_LANGUAGES (None) means unrestricted and is reserved for privileged users; an empty list is an empty scope, not a wildcard. Use this rather than reading AuthorizedTranslator.allowed_languages directly: it folds in the is_privileged_user short-circuit and the EMPTY_ALLOWED_LANGUAGES_MEANS_ALL setting, and branch on `is not None` so the two never collapse into one another.

surface.name: is_privileged_user
surface.intent: Whether a user is staff or superuser — the shortcut every other check here (get_user_allowed_languages, etc.) short-circuits on before consulting AuthorizedTranslator. Reach for this instead of writing user.is_superuser or user.is_staff inline so the privilege definition stays in one place.

surface.name: agent_payload
surface.intent: The llm.complete request body shared by AgentProvider and CommAgentProvider (model size + optional provider override). Reuse this when writing a third stapel-agent-backed provider instead of re-reading AGENT_MODEL_SIZE/AGENT_PROVIDER by hand.

surface.name: extract_agent_result
surface.intent: Parse the {status, result} envelope stapel-agent returns (HTTP or comm alike) into cleaned text, raising TranslationProviderError on a non-ok status or an empty/malformed result. Explicitly the shared HTTP/comm parsing step (per its own docstring) — reuse it in any custom provider that talks to stapel-agent through a different transport instead of re-deriving the envelope shape.

surface.name: get_agent_url
surface.intent: Base URL of the stapel-agent service (AGENT_SERVICE_URL, trailing slash stripped). Use this instead of reading translate_settings.AGENT_SERVICE_URL directly when writing a custom LLM_PROVIDER that still talks to stapel-agent, so the normalization stays in one place.

surface.name: get_llm_provider
surface.intent: Instantiate the configured LLM_PROVIDER. Call this instead of importing a specific provider class directly whenever custom code (a management command, a one-off script) needs to run a translation exactly the way autofill/LLM-help do.

surface.name: decode_screenshot
surface.intent: Turn a base64 screenshot into bounded, sniffed, decoder-verified bytes, or raise ScreenshotRejected. Every bound runs before the next step does any work — encoded length, decoded length, magic bytes, then header dimensions — so call this instead of base64.b64decode() in any endpoint that accepts an uploaded image; the naive decode is what let arbitrary bytes be written to disk as a .png.

surface.name: figma_url_allowed_hosts
surface.intent: The configured hosts a Figma ref may point at (FIGMA_URL_ALLOWED_HOSTS, normalised). Use it to render a helpful rejection message or a deployment check; validate_figma_url is what you call to actually decide.

surface.name: is_safe_href
surface.intent: Whether a stored string may go into an href/src without enabling script — an allowlist of http/https/mailto plus root-relative paths, normalised the way a browser normalises a scheme. Call this (or the |safe_href template filter) on any URL that came from the database or a peer service: Django's autoescaping protects the text of a value but happily keeps a javascript: scheme inside href="{{ ... }}".

surface.name: safe_href
surface.intent: The URL if is_safe_href accepts it, else an empty string — the value to actually interpolate into an href. Reach for this rather than escaping or regex-stripping a URL yourself; an empty href is inert, a half-sanitised one is not. In templates use the |safe_href filter from {% load stapel_translate %}.

surface.name: validate_figma_url
surface.intent: Return an HTTPS Figma-host URL unchanged, or raise UnsafeUrl. This is the write-boundary check every Figma ingestion endpoint runs before a ref reaches the database — call it in any custom endpoint that accepts a figma_url instead of trusting the plugin, so a poisoned ref is never stored for every other consumer to render.

surface.name: cache_key
surface.intent: The Django cache key one translated string is stored under — a digest of (version, source, target, context hint, text), so it is memcached-safe where the text itself is not. Reach for this to warm the cache ahead of traffic or to invalidate a single translation; never rebuild the key by hand, because a mismatch is a silent second bill rather than an error.

surface.name: check_bounds
surface.intent: Apply TEXT_MAX_CHARS / TEXT_BATCH_MAX_ITEMS / TEXT_BATCH_MAX_CHARS to a list of texts, raising TextTranslationRefused with the code that says which ceiling was hit. Call this before queueing texts for translation in custom code so a caller learns the input is too long before anything is spent on it, rather than after.

surface.name: check_language
surface.intent: Validate a language code against the deployment's configured languages, raising TextTranslationRefused rather than passing an unknown tag to the provider. Use it instead of an `in get_supported_languages()` check when the refusal has to reach an API caller as a localizable code.

surface.name: translate_texts
surface.intent: Translate arbitrary content — one string or a batch of short ones — through the configured LLM_PROVIDER, with the length ceilings, the language validation and the result cache already applied. This is what POST translate/api/v1/text/ runs; call it directly (a management command, a bulk backfill, a listing indexer) instead of reaching for get_llm_provider().translate(), which is the UI-string-KEY contract and applies none of the bounds. Raises TextTranslationRefused for anything the caller can fix.

requires.reason: comm bus (translate.resolve Function, translations.changed emit, task_handler), RevisionMixin, access categories, error registry (pyproject.toml dependency)

default LLM_PROVIDER (AgentProvider) calls stapel-agent over HTTP (AGENT_SERVICE_URL) or via the llm.complete comm Function (CommAgentProvider); no direct Python import either way (conf.py AGENT_SERVICE_URL, MODULE.md Settings table)
